description: Partial update of a tool page — only supplied fields change. endpointUrl: The client's own backend URL PostKing POSTs (or GETs, per endpointMethod) form submissions to, as { toolSlug, runId, inputs, visitor }, header "Authorization: Bearer {apiKey}". Omit or pass null for kind "none" — a pure lead-capture tool with no backend call; execute then skips the forward and the result is just the visitor's own inputs echoed back through resultTemplate/handoffUrl. apiKey: Write-only. Sent as the endpointUrl's Authorization: Bearer token; never echoed back by any tool_* response — those expose apiKeyLast4 (last 4 characters, or null) instead. resultTemplate: Mustache-style HTML rendered against the client endpoint's JSON response and the visitor's own submitted inputs. Placeholders: {{path.to.value}} (dotted path into the response JSON) and {{input.<key>}} (a submitted form value, e.g. {{input.email}}). No loops or conditionals — {{#if}}/{{#each}} are left as literal text. A missing value renders as "" (never the literal placeholder). Sanitized server-side on write (script tags, inline handlers, and iframes are stripped/rejected) — placeholders survive sanitization intact. When null, the renderer falls back to legacy resultType (json/text/url) rendering. Publish only after tool_preview shows an empty missingKeys array. handoffMode: "result": show the rendered resultTemplate with a Continue button pointing at the filled handoffUrl (hidden when handoffUrl is null). "redirect": skip the result screen and redirect immediately once the response (or, for async tools, the poll) resolves. handoffUrl: Where the visitor is sent after (or instead of) the result. Same {{path.to.value}} / {{input.<key>}} placeholder syntax as resultTemplate, URL-encoded — e.g. "https://client.com/signup?score={{score}}&email={{input.email}}". The client endpoint's own JSON response may include a top-level "redirectUrl" field, which overrides this at render time. layout: Public page layout. Defaults to "split". "split": copy-led, any number of inputSchema fields. "video": a walkthrough replaces the description; drops chips/deliverables/the sample band entirely, and the tool cannot be published without layoutConfig.videoUrl set. "product": dark hero with a screenshot up front; renders exactly ONE input field — extra inputSchema entries are silently dropped by the renderer. failureMessage: Shown to the visitor when the endpoint call fails. null (default): the renderer's own generic failure copy. usageCountStart: Seeds the displayed usage counter — the public usageCount is this value plus real executions. Non-negative integer. isPublished is accepted here but prefer tool_publish — it fires the same publish hooks (llms.txt, IndexNow, link graph) without resending the whole tool body.

apiKey.description: Write-only. Sent as the endpointUrl's Authorization: Bearer token; never echoed back by any tool_* response — those expose apiKeyLast4 (last 4 characters, or null) instead.

endpointUrl.description: The client's own backend URL PostKing POSTs (or GETs, per endpointMethod) form submissions to, as { toolSlug, runId, inputs, visitor }, header "Authorization: Bearer {apiKey}". Omit or pass null for kind "none" — a pure lead-capture tool with no backend call; execute then skips the forward and the result is just the visitor's own inputs echoed back through resultTemplate/handoffUrl.

failureMessage.description: Shown to the visitor when the endpoint call fails. null (default): the renderer's own generic failure copy.

handoffMode.description: "result": show the rendered resultTemplate with a Continue button pointing at the filled handoffUrl (hidden when handoffUrl is null). "redirect": skip the result screen and redirect immediately once the response (or, for async tools, the poll) resolves.

handoffUrl.description: Where the visitor is sent after (or instead of) the result. Same {{path.to.value}} / {{input.<key>}} placeholder syntax as resultTemplate, URL-encoded — e.g. "https://client.com/signup?score={{score}}&email={{input.email}}". The client endpoint's own JSON response may include a top-level "redirectUrl" field, which overrides this at render time.

inputSchema.description: The form fields the visitor fills in. product layout keeps only the first one — see layout.

key.description: Form field name — also the key inputs are submitted under and read via {{input.<key>}} in templates.

type.description: Input type: text, number, email, url, select, or textarea.

isPublished.description: Prefer tool_publish for this — see the tool description.

layout.description: Public page layout. Defaults to "split". "split": copy-led, any number of inputSchema fields. "video": a walkthrough replaces the description; drops chips/deliverables/the sample band entirely, and the tool cannot be published without layoutConfig.videoUrl set. "product": dark hero with a screenshot up front; renders exactly ONE input field — extra inputSchema entries are silently dropped by the renderer.

layoutConfig.description: Layout-specific page content for whichever `layout` the tool uses. Unknown/irrelevant keys for the current layout are simply not rendered — see each key's own description for which layout(s) it applies to.

chips.description: Short capability pills under the lede. split only.

deliverables.description: The numbered "what comes back" list on the form card. split only.

deliverablesTitle.description: Heading above the deliverables list. Defaults to "What comes back". split only.

eyebrow.description: Small mono label above the headline, e.g. "Free tool · No card needed". All layouts.

formCaption.description: Caption under the submit button, e.g. "Results in ~20s · no signup wall". All layouts.

formHeadline.description: Heading on the form card itself, e.g. "Run your scan". split and video.

formSubcopy.description: One line under the form heading, to excuse skipping the video. video only.

logoUrls.description: Customer logo wall beside the pull quote. product only.

sampleCopy.description: Lede of the sample-report band. split only.

sampleHeadline.description: Heading of the sample-report band. split only.

sampleImageAssetId.description: The library asset behind sampleImageUrl (editor-only; the renderer never reads it). split and product.

sampleImageKind.description: Whether sampleImageUrl is an image or a video. Defaults to image. split and product.

sampleImageUrl.description: The artifact screenshot or short video of it. split and product.

sampleMetrics.description: Up to three headline figures beside the sample heading. split only.

showDeliverables.description: false hides the deliverables list entirely. Defaults to true. split only.

steps.description: The three-step hairline grid. product only — exactly three reads best.

submitLabel.description: The submit button's label. Defaults to "Run". All layouts.

videoAssetId.description: The library asset behind videoUrl. video only.

videoControls.description: Whether a video slot shows native player controls. Defaults to true. Applies to video always, and to split/product when sampleImageKind is "video".

videoDurationLabel.description: Overlaid on the player, e.g. "0:58 · sound optional". video only.

videoPosterAssetId.description: The library asset behind videoPosterUrl. video only.

videoPosterUrl.description: Poster frame for the video player. video only.

videoUrl.description: The walkthrough video that replaces the description. video only — REQUIRED before a video-layout tool can publish.

Placeholders: {{path.to.value}} (dotted path into the response JSON) and {{input.<key>}} (a submitted form value, e.g. {{input.email}}). No loops or conditionals — {{#if}}/{{#each}} are left as literal text. A missing value renders as "" (never the literal placeholder). Sanitized server-side on write (script tags, inline handlers, and iframes are stripped/rejected) — placeholders survive sanitization intact. When null, the renderer falls back to legacy resultType (json/text/url) rendering. Publish only after tool_preview shows an empty missingKeys array.

usageCountStart.description: Seeds the displayed usage counter — the public usageCount is this value plus real executions. Non-negative integer.
